entradas.text: The Maroon Palace was bustling with activity as party leaders and their entourages filed in one by one to discuss the latest changes to the constitutional reform proposal.
Inside the presidential office, the tension was thick in the air, and the sound of hushed whispers filled the room.
I shifted in my seat, scanning the room as the leaders of the USP -- with Gloria Tory in the front -- walked in.
"Gentlemen, Ms. Tory, thank you for coming. I trust you all received the latest version of the reform proposal?"
"I understand there has been some concern about the latest additions to the reform proposal. Please, have a seat and let's discuss this like rational adults."
The party leaders exchanged wary glances before taking their seats.
entradas.menu: Wait for everyone to get seated.

entradas.text: The party leaders exchanged wary glances before taking their seats.
"We did. And we have some concerns."
"But today, Ms. Tory will be speaking on behalf of the party."
"Mr. President, thank you for having us. But today, Ms. Tory will be speaking on behalf of the party."
"Yes. Let's do that."
"Did all the wings of the party suddenly decide to band together? If I'd known this is what it took, I would have added these changes sooner."
"I thought all of you had your own personal opinions and concerns about this. This is the time for you to speak your minds -- each and every one of you."
"Very well. Let's begin. Shall we, Ms. Tory?"
"Then why did you come here all together? She could have represented you by herself."
"Very funny, Mr. Rayne."
"We discussed everything in detail before coming here. The party has chosen me as their spokesperson."
"Well, Mr. Rayne..."
"I think it's fair to say we're all here because we're deeply concerned about the recent changes you've made to the reform proposal."
"I think it's fair to say we're all here because we're deeply concerned about the way you're trying to push the party in a direction its own members don't approve of."
"Especially after the whole party gave you the necessary signatures to open the constitutional reform process."
"Especially after I collected the necessary signatures to open the constitutional reform process."
"I understand your concerns, but I stand by my decision. Let's talk about how I can convince you to support me."
"I made the changes because I believe they are necessary. Our proposal wouldn't be a proper democratic reform if it didn't include changes to the discriminatory Article 6 and Article 7."
"You can't just make changes like this at the last minute. We had a deal, and you've gone and changed the terms of it without any consultation."
"There is a reason behind my decision. Let me explain and I'm sure you will approve."

"The circumstances have changed. You know about the incidents in Bergia and the Supreme Court's attitude on this topic. As the administration, we are responsible for protecting the rights of our Bludish citizens."
She leaned forward, her hands gripping the table's edge tightly.
Her voice was taut with anger.
"Oh?"
"After you realized you didn't have my support, you made changes to win over some Bludish and liberal voters, plain and simple."
"You already knew you had no support from the party. Yet you push this ridiculous change at the last minute, knowing you will fail."
"You are trying to bring the USP down with you, Mr. Rayne. And this is your plan to destroy our legacy and legitimacy. Plain and simple."
Her voice was taut with anger.
"Either you're proving to be a worse politician than President Alphonso or this is your plan to destroy our legacy and legitimacy."
"You're still continuing with this?"
"It seems you don't understand, Mr. President."
"We didn't organize this meeting for you to convince us. On the contrary, we are here to confront you and make sure you understand your current position within the USP."
"You may be the president of this republic, Mr. Rayne. But know this: you lost the support of the party."
"Mr. Rayne. I'm not sure if you understand. You can't sweet talk your way out of this."
"The whole party is *extremely* disappointed with your additions. Removing the very foundational concept of this country? You know what that means."
"And you're acting as if that's the only violation of our agreement."
"I thought I was very clear when I told you not to pursue privatization of healthcare or the Sordish State Corporation."
"And you went ahead and started to process for both!"
"But you went ahead with opening our healthcare for privatization anyway."
"But you went against the SSC anyway."
"I'm not going to let you ridicule me and the party any longer, Mr. Rayne. If my words mean nothing to you, so be it."
"Come on, Ms. Tory. Let's be reasonable."
"What is the meaning of this?"
"You are not the USP, Ms. Tory. You can't speak on behalf of everyone like this."
"Are you really planning to convince us by violating our agreements and confronting us with a surprise reform package that includes changes that go against the values of the party?"
"Oh, but I can."
"I thought I already told you that the party is united on this topic and they have chosen me as their spokesperson."
"No need to look for hidden meanings, Mr. Rayne."
"I thought I was very clear."
"You've chosen force over reason, Mr. Rayne. You will not find any more reason in us."
The leaders of the USP watched us in silence with weathered faces. Albin Clavin didn't make any eye contact.
"Mr. Clavin, how about you? I trust that you still support me and the administration."
"Is nobody else going to speak?"
"So, you're saying the USP will unanimously vote against the proposal? After all this hard work?"
"Man up, gentlemen! Don't let Ms. Tory take the helm of your ship! Say something. I'm sure some of you have differing opinions."
He nodded in disagreement but did not respond.
None of the leaders in the room responded.
"You should have thought about your hard work before pushing us into a corner."
"Mr. Rayne. Your time with this party is through."
"You can't be that naive, Mr. Rayne. We suspect you have different ambitions."
"What different ambitions, Ms. Tory? What are you insinuating?"
"You're right, I'm not that naive. I wouldn't have gone with this if I didn't believe we could pass it."
"My only ambition is to democratize Sordland and erase the inherent discrimination from our constitution."
"The party should respect my decision for once. Why would protecting the rights of the Bludish people be against the USP? Are we not representing everyone in this country?"
"Before asking for respect, you should have respected the decision of the people that gave you that seat, Mr. Rayne. You are forgetting where you're coming from."
"We represent all Sords in Sordland and beyond. You know this very well. And despite that, you're trying to shift the meaning of 'Sord' and portray it as a purely ethnic term."
"You are creating a needless stir over this topic and deflecting from the real problems of this country."
"Did you mean to say 'divide Sordland'? You are literally trying to legitimize the secessionists and their goals."
"It sounds like you are trying to legitimize the secessionists and their goals, Mr. Rayne."
"Do you want us to believe that?"
"You didn't even let me explain anything. I'm not with the secessionists. In fact, I have a plan to stop them for good."
"Am I the one who's deflecting? Are you really going to ignore the discrimination our Bludish citizens face in Sordland?"
"Tell me. What can I do for you? Is there nothing that will convince you otherwise?"
"Not when you're betraying the values of our party and republic."
"Are you really ignoring the discrimination our Bludish citizens face in Sordland?"
"What betrayal? This country is built on unity. My proposal would only strengthen that."
"Unity? Our constitution -- albeit flawed -- does not refer to any subdivisions of our nation. Every citizen is equal and united under one flag, one nation and one language."
"Removing Sord from Sordland would only destroy this country. Is this not an attack against this nation, Mr. Rayne?"
"You are acknowledging the aims of the secessionists by agreeing with their baseless arguments. Are you really claiming Article 6 is what started the terror?"
"Don't make us laugh, Mr. Rayne."
"Don't try to pin that on Article 6. This is about what this country is, about Sords and about unity."
She snorted derisively.
"Fine. I'm listening."
"How is enshrining equal rights for everyone against this nation, Mr. Tory? I didn't expect you to be this blinded by ethno-nationalism."
"This would only make our Bludish citizens feel more accepted. It is the only way to fight the BFF."
"The Bludish community wants to be recognized by the state. We should no longer ignore their culture and identity."
"Don't throw words around like that. I'm not a supporter of anti-Bludism and I'm definitely not what you're labeling me as."
"And the constitution already grants equal rights to everyone."
"What is your problem with the Bludish people?"
"If the USP won't vote for this proposal, the PFJP would jump on the opportunity and take all the credit. We will lose our the entirety of what's left of our Bludish base."
"I'm not saying Article 6 is the sole cause, but it's one of the reasons nonetheless. If millions of Bludish people demand this change, we should listen to them."
"We are talking past each other at this stage. I'm done with this meeting, Mr. Rayne. It seems you have nothing but BFF propaganda to talk about."
"I'm not going to let you ridicule me and the party any longer. If my words mean nothing to you, so be it."
"Please. Have reason, Ms. Tory. This is the 20th century, we must leave our racist tendencies behind."
"Please, let's calm down. I have something that can end the BFF once and for all. Let me explain."
"The party will evolve, whether you like it or not."
"Evolve? You mean erase our identity?"
"So, accepting everyone as Sords regardless of their ethnicity instead of dividing the nation into subgroups is racist?"
"So be it, Ms. Tory."
"Mr. Clavin, how about you? You call yourself a reformist, don't you? This is the time to act like one."

"The BFF lost the support of the Bludish people. We have new channels of intelligence about them, their plans and their leadership. If this proposal goes through, the Bludish movement will aid us in destroying them."
"Fetih Ejall is offering a cooperation against the BFF in exchange for the changes."
"By listening to the demands of our Bludish citizens, we will earn their loyalty. The BFF is on the decline and we have new intelligence that can potentially end them."
"So you are cooperating with the terrorists, after all."
"What is the source of this *new* intelligence?"
"The Bludish democratic movement is aiding us."
"The Workers' Party is offering a cooperation against the BFF in exchange for the changes."
"The Workers Party of Bludia?"
She bristled with disgust.
"So the rumors were true... And this is why Ms. Graf and her staff were in such a rush. Is the operation underway, at least?"
"They are being monitored and the ministry will be receiving the intelligence as we get it."
"The planning phase is underway. I'm sure we'll get them soon as we receive more information."
"I'll be clear. If we don't try to pass this change, we may lose the cooperation of the Bludish movement. Which we need until the end."
"And you are letting them withhold information from us, in exchange for our support?"
"This is frankly ridiculous."
"Look. The intel we received so far has been reliable. Even Ms. Graf has confirmed this. We can't let go of this chance."
"The secessionists are one of the Sollists' primary concerns, are they not? With this plan, we can eliminate them and earn the loyalty of our Bludish citizens. Is this not the unity the USP desire?"
"Please stop with this attitude, Ms. Tory. They deserve to be recognized. The BFF didn't appear out of nowhere. Did you ever ask yourselves if maybe you're to blame?"
"There is an important offer I need to explain. It will change your perspective."
"You did not just say that."
"We are talking past each other at this stage. I'm done with this meeting, Mr. Rayne. It seems you have nothing but BFF propaganda to talk about."
"I'm not going to let you ridicule me and the party any longer, Mr. Rayne. If my words mean nothing to you, so be it."
I've heard hushed whispers among the party leaders.
"Perhaps."
She turned her back and joined the whispering.
I waited in silence until they finished their discussion.
entradas.menu: Wait.

entradas.text: "Ms. Tory, gentlemen, I am right in front of you. You can talk directly to me."
Nobody responded. Gloria turned to me after they finished their discussion.
"Eliminating the BFF is surely a high priority for the party, Mr. Rayne. But this is not the way."

"We can see how these changes would boost our popularity among the Bludish people. But without the elimination of the secessionist movement, this does no good for the nation. And that could backfire at any time."
"In order for us to even start talking about a possible deal, you have to first remove your changes to the election threshold and reinstate the Member of Honor rights for Tarquin Soll."
"What are your concerns? Let's try to find some common ground."
"Is there something I can offer to make you happy?"
"I'm sure we can make a deal."
"I don't think there's much we can compromise on, Mr. Rayne."
"I'm not against these changes in principle, but the political reality is different."
"But perhaps we could still work something out."
"In order for us to even start talking about a possible deal, you have to first remove your changes to the election threshold."
"In order for us to even start talking about a possible deal, you have to first remove your changes to the Member of Honor rights of Tarquin Soll."
"Will that ensure your support?"
"Fine. I'll remove them if we end up making a deal today."
entradas.menu: "Fine. I'll remove them if we end up making a deal today." [REMOVE CHANGES FROM PROPOSAL]

entradas.text: "But you already agreed to those points, Ms. Tory. Please don't be unreasonable."
"Am I the one who ignored our deal and tried to force the party to accept my last-minute changes?"
"So, what is it going to be?"
"No. It won't. This is only the proposal, Mr. Rayne. We may yet have other requests."
"No. I can't do that."
"Will that ensure your support?"
"Fine. I'll remove it if we end up making a deal today."
entradas.menu: "Fine. I'll remove it if we end up making a deal today." [REMOVE CHANGE FROM PROPOSAL]

entradas.text: "But you already agreed to that point before, Ms. Tory. Please don't be unreasonable."
"Am I the one who ignored our deal and tried to force the party to follow my last-minute changes?"
"So, what is it going to be?"
"No. It won't. This is only the proposal, Mr. Rayne. We may yet have other requests."
"No. I can't do that. There will be no deals."
"Will that ensure your support?"
"Fine. I'll remove it if we end up making a deal today."
entradas.menu: "Fine. I'll remove it if we end up making a deal today." [REMOVE CHANGE FROM PROPOSAL]

entradas.text: "But you already agreed to that point before, Ms. Tory. Please don't be unreasonable."
"Am I the one who ignored our deal and tried to force the party to agree on my last-minute changes?"
"So, what is it going to be?"
"No. It won't. This is only the proposal, Mr. Rayne. We may have other requests."
"No. I can't do that. There will be no deals."
"Then it's time for us to leave. There won't be any deals."
"This is a mistake."
"Then it's time for us to leave."
"Then it's time for us to leave."
"This is a mistake."
"This is a mistake."
"Good."
"Good."
"Good."
"Now, let's talk about how you can make amends with our party."
"The USP is not happy with the changes you made to the Energy Protection Act. You turned it into an Energy Exploitation Act."
"The USP is not happy with the removal of the Energy Protection Act."
"The party is not happy with Ewald Alphonso's changes to the Energy Protection Act. Which you did nothing to reverse."
"You opened the way for foreign powers to control half of our energy industry. This is not something we can accept."
You opened way for the foreign powers to control our energy industry. This is not something we can accept."
"This is not something we can accept."
"We were absolutely furious to learn about your plans to give semi-autonomy to Bergia."
"We want a reversal to the 10% allowance of the Tarquin Soll era."
"You will immediately stop all your work on the re-structuring of the Special Zone."
She looked me dead in the eye.
"After we confirm the integrity of the intelligence, you will arrest Fetih Ejall for harboring connections to the BFF and withholding information from the state."
"And after we confirm the integrity of the intelligence, you will arrest Fetih Ejall for harboring connections to the BFF and withholding information from the state."
"If you can do that, we'll have a deal."
"Mr. Ejall is helping us. I can't agree to arrest him. This conflicts with our aim of earning the support of the Bludish populace."
"I can't agree to reverting the Energy Protection Act. We need foreign capital."
"Fine. I agree to all of your demands. I'll revert the Energy Protection Act, cancel the semi-autonomous zone and arrest Mr. Ejall."
entradas.menu: "Fine. I agree to all of your demands. I'll revert the Energy Protection Act, cancel the semi-autonomous zone and arrest Mr. Ejall." [CONFIRM DEAL]

entradas.text: "I can't stop the work on the semi-autonomous zone now. This goes hand in hand with our reform proposal."
"So you agree with our other demands?"
"Revert the Energy Protection Act and cancel the work on the semi-autonomous zone and we'll have a deal."
"That will simply not work, Mr. Rayne."
"Fine. We'll arrest Fetih Ejall."
entradas.menu: "Fine. We'll arrest Fetih Ejall." [CONFIRM DEAL]

entradas.text: "Either you agree with our demands or there is no deal."
"Deal. I'll do those two, but we'll spare Mr. Ejall."
entradas.menu: "Deal. I'll do those two, but we'll spare Mr. Ejall." [CONFIRM DEAL]

entradas.text: "So you agree with our other demands?"
"Cancel the work on the semi-autonomous zone and arrest Ejall and we'll have a deal."
"Deal. I'll do those two, and we won't touch the Energy Act."
entradas.menu: "Deal. I'll do those two, and we won't touch the Energy Act." [CONFIRM DEAL]

entradas.text: "That is a red line for us, Mr. Rayne. You have to stop it."
"We can't simply leave Bergia as it is. How about this? I'll stop the semi-autonomous zone and we'll go with Ms. Graf's plan to abolish the Special Zone instead."
"I can't do that."
"I can't do that."
"You're putting too much pressure on me, Ms. Tory."
"I'm sorry but I don't think there will be a deal."
"You know what? If you're willing to do that, we'll have a deal."
"Deal. I'll push for the abolishment of the Special Zone and the centralization of Bergia."
entradas.menu: "Deal. I'll push for the abolishment of the Special Zone and the centralization of Bergia." [CONFIRM DEAL]

entradas.text: "On second thought, I'm not really sure."
"Fine. I agree to all of your demands. I'll cancel the semi-autonomous zone and order the arrest of Mr. Ejall."
entradas.menu: "Fine. I agree to all of your demands. I'll cancel the semi-autonomous zone and order the arrest of Mr. Ejall." [CONFIRM DEAL]

entradas.text: "Fine. I agree to all of your demands. I'll revert the Energy Protection Act and order the arrest of Mr. Ejall."
entradas.menu: "Fine. I agree to all of your demands. I'll revert the Energy Protection Act and order the arrest of Mr. Ejall." [CONFIRM DEAL]

entradas.text: "Then you can get your support from elsewhere, Mr. Rayne."
"Then you can get your support from elsewhere, Mr. Rayne."
"I'm sure you can take it."
She sighed.
"Then we have a deal."
She nodded in approval and reached out for a handshake.
"I hope you respect it this time."
"If you say so, Mr. Rayne. You can say goodbye to your reform package."
She sighed.
She stood up and turned to the leaders of the party.
"Gentlemen, we have another Alphonso in our hands. You know what to do."
She then turned to me and reached her hand for a handshake.
"Thank you for the meeting regardless."
We shook hands.
entradas.menu: Shake her hand.

entradas.text: I did not offer my hand nor responded to her.
entradas.menu: Don't do anything.

entradas.text: "Look. I apologize for everything. Give me one more chance. I can remove the changes to Article 6 and 7. Let's act as if nothing happened."
"Please don't embarrass yourself any longer. You still carry the name of the party."
She bellowed out a laughter.
She smirked dismissively.
"Have a good day, Mr. Rayne."
"Not even a gesture of respect... Please don't embarrass yourself any longer, Mr. Rayne. You still carry the name of the party."
She, together with the rest of the leadership and their entourage, left the room with slow steps.
It seemed my own party had abandoned me.
After shaking hands, Gloria, together with the rest of the leadership and their entourage, left the office.
A few minutes later, Petr joined me inside.
"So, how did it go?"
"Good luck finding votes for your *reforms.* Not even your pert vice president can help you with it now."
"So, how did it go?"
"The USP has united against me, Petr..."
"To be completely honest, I think we're screwed."
"I'm sorry, Petr. I think I pushed the party too far. We may need to say goodbye to our reforms."
"They showed their true faces and abandoned us for dead. We need to make a plan. We can't let them smear and destroy the administration."
"Shit..."
"I told you we can't trust anyone except each other, Anton. We knew we were always on our own."
"But don't worry. We'll find a way out of this. Just like we always have."
"I wish I could be that optimistic."
"Thank you, Petr. Your support means a lot to me."
"It's going to be difficult with the USP breathing down our necks."
"Come on, Anton. How many hopeless situations have we found ourselves in before? Every single time, we managed to weather the storm."
For a second, I sensed desperation in his eyes.
"This is bad."
He plastered on a forceful smile.
"You know I'll always be there for you, Anton."
He put his hand on my shoulder.
"Lighten up now."
"Amazing. The whole party promised to vote for the proposal."
"They pushed me around and I had to compromise, but it worked out in the end."
"We made a deal, but I still don't trust them. It looked like they were uniting against us."
"It didn't go as planned. We made a deal, but it seems like the party is uniting under Ms. Tory now. She may be their next candidate."
"I suspect she's the decoy, Anton. Whoever the real contender is, they're waiting for the right moment to come out."
"She's a central figure, but I doubt the party considers her candidate material."
"I was suspecting the same. There is a lot of movement in the party these days."
"They may be organizing behind a new contender for leadership. And whoever that person is, they're waiting for the right moment to come out."
"You did it!?"
"If we can really pass these reforms, you'll be making history."
"But for now, we should focus on our next steps. If we can actually pass these reforms, you'll be making history."
"That's a relief."
Petr took a look at his watch.
"Oh, there is another thing. Frens wanted to talk to you about the new changes before the vote as well."
"I took the liberty of inviting him to join us after your meeting with the party. He should be here soon."
"Great. As if the party wasn't enough... I hope he didn't change his mind as well."
"I'm sure he'll be delighted hear the whole USP is behind the proposal."
Petr took a look at his watch.
"I don't know if you forgot, but Frens wanted to talk to you about the proposal as well. Don't show any weakness in front of him."
"I took the liberty of inviting him to join us after your meeting with the party. He should be here soon."
"Good. I want to get this over with before the vote."
"Great. As if the party wasn't enough... I don't know if the PFJP can even help us anymore."
"I'm sure he'll be delighted hear the whole USP will be boycotting the proposal."
"Good. I want to get it over with this before the vote."
"I think he's aware of the division in our party, Anton. I suspect he has ears in these halls."
"As much as he may act disappointed, I think deep inside he was craving for this to happen, so he could blame us for the failure."
"After all, our failure to deliver reforms will only strengthen the PFJP."
"I don't care about Frens or the PFJP anymore. The party has already thrown our reforms into the trash."
"Honestly, I'd rather have them lead the reforms than our party. I hope to be the last USP president in this country."
"Are you saying he knew this would happen?"
"Yes. He probably even planned it from the very beginning."
"There is s--"
"Are you serious?"
"Don't be like that, Anton. It is not the end of the world. We're still here, aren't we?"
Suddenly, Livia informed us about Frens Ricter's arrival.
On my gesture, Frens entered the office. After shaking hands, we sat down on the sofas.
I picked it up. Livia told me that Frens Ricter was on the line.
"With the majority behind the reforms, I don't think he can afford a sudden change of heart."
"He already supported the reforms, and the latest additions were something he's been campaigning for."
"I doubt that, Anton. I believe -- deep down inside -- he wants us to fail, so he can blame us for the failure and take the helm."
"After all, our failure to deliver reforms will only strengthen the PFJP."
"But of course, with the majority behind the reforms, I don't think he can afford a sudden change of heart."
Suddenly, the phone rang.
"Let's get some fresh air. There's not much we can do about the reforms now."
"The President speaking."
"Hello, Mr. Ricter."
"What do you want?"
"Did you forget how to show respect, Mr. Rayne?"
"It seems you're showing your true colors since our meeting didn't go according to your plan."
"I should have seen your true colors when you tried to cooperate with Mr. Kibener."
"Good day, Mr. Rayne."
"Anyway... I'm calling to let you know that your sneaky little scheme won't work on us."
"I'm calling to let you know that your sneaky little plan won't work on us."
"I know what you're doing. You think you can pressure us by adding our proposed changes to Article 6 and 7."
"Everybody can see what this proposal intends to do as a whole. You cannot deceive anybody by adding a few lines of so-called democratization."
"We will not fall for your trap."
"What are you talking about, Mr. Ricter? There is no trap here. You're being paranoid."
"I thought you wanted to add these changes to the proposal. What's the issue now?"
"Come on, Mr. Ricter. The USP is willing to support the reforms you want. Are you really going to abandon your agenda all of a sudden?"
"You're bluffing. I've heard there is a division among the PFJP. Do you really want me to believe you are in complete control?"
"I thought you wanted me to add these changes to the proposal. What's the issue now?"
"Come on, Mr. Ricter. The USP is willing to support the reforms you want. Are you really going to abandon your reformist agenda all of a sudden?"
"The *reformist* agenda? Are you serious?"
"I never cooperated with you on the reform proposal, Mr. Rayne. Adding two points from our campaign won't suddenly undo everything else in your package."
"You think I'm stupid?"
"Believe what you will, Mr. Rayne."
"We won't be forced into cooperation. You are watering down our ideals and presenting our hard work as your own. I won't let the PFJP be your lapdog."
"Sooner or later, everybody will realize that no true democratic reform will be a reality as long as your party is in charge."
"I should have known you were a man who'd let go of tangible reforms for political gains."
"So you never cared about the reforms and it was all a strategy to increase your power base, is that it?"
"Let's calm down, Mr. Ricter. Why don't we arrange a meeting to discuss this in detail?"
"Mr. President. Mr. Vice President. It's good to see you."
"Don't try to spin things your way. You know exactly what I mean."
"It's too late for that, Mr. Rayne."
"I'll see you at next week's vote."
"Have a nice day."
"No, Petr. You go ahead. I'm not in the mood."
"You're right. Let's go."
"But what about you? What do you think will happen with our reforms?"
"Come on, Anton. You need to let go of this stress a little."
"You already know that without the USP there is no way of passing the Assembly. But I told you that it would be very risky, Anton."
"Let's not overthink this. Let's get some fresh air, shall we?"
"Judging by the conversations I've overheard in the Palace, I assume the USP cannot be trusted to pass the reforms anymore?"
"I hope everything is going well with the preparations for the vote next week."
"I hope all the bribery you've done won't go to waste."
"Come to think of it, your connection with the Oligarchs may still help us salvage the situation."
"Of course we will."
"Well, you heard wrong."
"Unfortunately, it's true. Your suggested amendments to the citizenship section lost us the USP."
"Yes. Most of the party will likely vote against the proposal."
"Don't let rumors discourage you. As long as your party gives its complete support, there is always a possibility of passing it."
"Yes. It looks very promising."
"With your support, we will be making history, Mr. Ricter. You can count on the USP."
"There were a few misunderstandings, but everything is going well at the moment."
"Well... About that..."
Frens leaned backwards and looked at me squarely.
"You didn't mention more changes to the proposal. You know I support your latest additions to Article 6 and 7, but who gave you the authority to remove already agreed-upon terms?"
"On my way here, I learned you were suddenly removing the change to the election threshold. We've told you numerous times that a decrease to the threshold is a necessity."

"On my way here, I learned that you've suddenly decided to protect Tarquin Soll's Member of Honor privileges. We've told you numerous times that opening the door to putting Soll on trial is a necessity."
"On top of it, you also decided to protect Tarquin Soll's Member of Honor privileges."
"I must say I'm very disappointed about this, Mr. Rayne. You are putting me in a difficult spot."
"I cannot let you abuse our willingness to work with you. You cannot act like we are 'supposed to' support you no matter what."
"As expected. But discouraging nonetheless."
